chunks: I asked him about the ritual slaughter (dhakah). So he said: 'Do not slaughter except by iron. Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) forbade from that.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Amir al-Mu'minin — Commander of the Faithful, the title of Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him)
key_terms.الذَّكَاة: Dhakah — the Islamic requirement for lawful ritual slaughter that renders an animal's meat halal
key_terms.حَدِيدَة: Hadidah — iron; a specific metal implement required for performing valid Islamic slaughter

ai.seo_question: Must Islamic ritual slaughter be performed with iron according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Sama'ah ibn Mihran asked Imam al-Sadiq or Imam al-Kazim (peace be upon them) about the requirements for lawful slaughter (dhakah). The Imam stated that the slaughter must be performed using an iron implement, citing the prohibition of Amir al-Mu'minin Imam Ali (peace be upon him) against using other materials. This establishes iron as a necessary condition for halal slaughter in Shia jurisprudence, differentiating it from using stone, bone, or other materials.
